conventions.convention: Binary outcomes are dimensionless labels −1 and +1; settings are finite nonempty sets, specialized to I=J={0,1} for CHSH. S=E00+E01+E10−E11.

A local-response representation uses one probability space and one probability measure for every setting pair, with normalized measurable single-station response laws and the factorized integral identity. Responses may be stochastic.
Selection is conditioning on a measurable specification-space event D with P(D)>0, using the same D at every setting pair; the response laws remain unchanged.
The complex inner product is linear in its first argument. The ordered spin-half basis is (e+,e−), the singlet is (e+⊗e−−e−⊗e+)/√2, and P(a,ε)=(I+ε a·σ)/2 for unit a.

The arrangement uses two distinguishable internal spaces C², a density operator on their completed tensor product, and four explicitly declared product-projection measurements. Spin outcome coordinates are ±ℏ/2 in J s; sign correlations are dimensionless. Countable Choice and AC are assumed. No spatial separation, temporal order, apparatus realization or observation is assigned.

There are n trials per setting pair; all 4n outcome pairs are mutually independent, and within each setting pair their laws equal the declared table. Independence and repetition laws are additional sampling assumptions, not deductions from the state postulates.

load_bearing.statement: A local-response representation consists of one probability space and normalized measurable response laws αi and βj satisfying μij(ε,δ)=∫αi(λ,ε)βj(λ,δ)dP(λ) for every setting pair and outcome pair.

A declared spin correlation arrangement consists of the composite V⊗̂V of two declared spin-half factors, a declared density preparation ρ, and two unit setting directions per station. The declared joint sign measurements have projections P(ai,ε)⊗P(bj,δ), with probabilities tr(ρ(P(ai,ε)⊗P(bj,δ))).
Let μ be a binary correlation model on I=J={0,1} and suppose that μ admits a local-response representation. Then |S(μ)|≤2. No physical assumption and no choice principle is used.
Assume Countable Choice. For the stated normalized singlet and all unit a,b and ε,δ∈{−1,+1}, ⟨(P(a,ε)⊗P(b,δ))Ψ,Ψ⟩=(1−εδ a·b)/4; both marginals are 1/2 and the correlation is −a·b.

For a local-response representation and a measurable specification-space event D with P(D)>0, PD(A)=P(A∩D)/P(D) is a probability measure; the D-conditional tables are represented by the same response laws over PD and satisfy |S|≤2 when I=J={0,1}.

Under the declared arrangement and Countable Choice and AC, the singlet tables are (1−εδ ai·bj)/4. At a0=(0,0,1), a1=(1,0,0), b0=(1,0,1)/√2 and b1=(−1,0,1)/√2, S=−2√2, so these four tables admit no local-response model.

Under the declared mutually independent sampling model, E[Ŝ]=S, Var(Ŝ)≤4/n, and P(|Ŝ−S|≥ε)≤4/(nε²) for ε>0. Any acceptance criterion rejecting a sequence of positive product probability has positive failure probability.

concerns.concern: The Brunner reference says 'Section II.A, PDF pages 2-3'. In the opened https://arxiv.org/pdf/1303.2849, pages 2-3 contain Section I.A; Section II.A starts on page 5. The cited table vocabulary is supported, but the section locator is wrong.

The Brunner reference labels the two-station scenario on PDF pages 2-3 as 'Section II.A'. Those pages are Section I.A; Section II.A begins on page 5. The substantive scenario attribution is supported.
The Brunner reference says 'Section II.A, PDF page 3' for the local decomposition and setting independence. The opened PDF places equations (2)-(4) and this discussion in Section I.A on page 3.

The Brunner reference associates 'Section II.A and Section II.C' with PDF pages 2-4 and 8-13. The introductory local-model discussion on pages 2-4 is Section I.A; Section II.A begins on page 5. Correct the locator without changing the supported comparison scope.

The Source qualifications paragraph says 'no commutator estimate is used as a premise'. The cited mathematical Tsirelson supplier explicitly uses ||[A0,A1]||≤2 and ||[B0,B1]||≤2 in proof step 2.1, and the batch physics theorem invokes its resulting norm bound in F6/1.2. The bound is sound, but this description of its prerequisite argument is inaccurate.

alerts.finding: Facts & Assumptions F2 states, for 'bounded F and unit Ψ', that tr(TΨ,Ψ F)=⟨FΨ,Ψ⟩=||F^(1/2)Ψ||²≥0. Boundedness alone does not imply positivity: F=−I gives −1 on the left. The cited density/PVM supplier does not assert this for arbitrary bounded F. The theorem's actual effect applications are positive, but the fact as written is false.

The supplier's owning page, library/non-relativistic-quantum-mechanics-mathematics/qm-math-orbital-and-spin.md, says 'the standard matrices J_z e_m=me_m and J_± e_m=... are self-adjoint'. The item itself correctly states J_+*=J_−. For s=1/2, J_+ is the nonzero strictly upper-triangular matrix and is not self-adjoint. The page's self-adjointness description needs correction; the supplier proposition is sound.

Completed tensor maps, rank-one trace identities and density expansions are used within their domains and with Countable Choice.
P1/P2/P3/P6/P7 remain adopted assumptions; spin coordinates retain J s units and signs are dimensionless. No empirical input is invented.
Preparations are positive self-adjoint trace-class operators of trace one; the normalized singlet yields the stated pure preparation.
Spectral/Born outcome laws are used for explicitly assigned sharp quantities, preserving units and choice hypotheses.
The finite C² internal spin-half factor is explicitly isolated from the spatial L² factor; no position, worldline or dynamics is assigned to it.

The directional spin-half projections and ±ℏ/2 coordinates agree with the supplier; their finite internal-factor form is also justified by the Pauli algebra.
Product rank-one partial traces and finite independent-sampling identities retain the supplier hypotheses.

Basis-state projection weights follow the stated spin-half laws and direct Pauli diagonal pairings.
The example uses the actual finite Pauli identities and consistent basis ordering.
P7's independent repetition model is explicitly added; estimator probabilities and finite-record support statements remain conditional, with no reported experiment or empirical verdict.
